rules.name: General Evidence Correlation

direction.title: Expand Facial Recognition Search
direction.description: Cross-reference detected faces against criminal databases, social media, and recent arrest records. Even partial matches can reveal associates or prior convictions.
direction.trigger: A usable face is present in case evidence (photo/CCTV still).
cross_match: Face match candidates against other suspects/associates named in this case
direction.expected_outcome: Either an identity match, or a confirmed dead-end that rules out the 'known offender' angle and strengthens other hypotheses.

rules.why_template: Face evidence exists in case — facial recognition is the fastest path to identifying suspects or their associates.

rules.name: Digital / Destroyed-Storage Forensics

direction.title: Recover & Forensically Analyse Destroyed/Wiped Digital Storage
direction.description: If any device or storage medium was chemically destroyed, wiped, or physically damaged, identify exactly which devices, what data they likely held, whether a backup or cloud copy exists, and who had access before/after the destruction event.
direction.trigger: Evidence or case notes reference destroyed, wiped, or tampered digital storage/devices.
search_targets: Cloud backup accounts tied to those devices
Access logs immediately before and after the destruction event
cross_match: Pre/post-destruction access log against employee/suspect list
Backup content against what's now missing from the scene
direction.expected_outcome: Recovers a backup or partial data trail even when the primary device is destroyed, and identifies who had access at the time of destruction — a strong pointer toward insider involvement if internal access was required.

rules.why_template: Destroyed digital evidence is itself a lead — recovering even a partial backup, or identifying who had access when it was destroyed, can be as valuable as the original data.

rules.name: Telecom & Communications Pattern Analysis

direction.title: Analyse Telecom / Radio Communication Pattern
direction.description: If the scene shows coordinated behaviour (hand signals, short radio bursts, synchronised movement), pull lawfully available telecom records for the incident window and area: tower dumps, unusual/unregistered devices (burner phones), and any encrypted-app usage indicators.
direction.trigger: Evidence indicates coordinated multi-person activity (team movement, signalling, timed actions) suggesting real-time communication.
search_targets: Tower dump for the incident window and radius
Encrypted-app usage indicators where lawfully accessible
cross_match: Active devices in the window against known suspect numbers
Device movement pattern against the vehicle/escape route
direction.expected_outcome: Surfaces unidentified devices active only during the incident window — a strong signature of a coordinated, planned operation versus a lone or opportunistic actor.
failure_conditions: Encrypted app content not lawfully accessible

rules.why_template: Coordinated behaviour at the scene implies real-time communication — even without content access, device presence patterns alone can confirm or rule out a team operation.

rules.name: Financial / Digital Trail Check (cross-hypothesis)

direction.title: Check Financial Trail Even If Motive Isn't Primarily Financial
direction.description: Financial evidence (wallet, transaction reference, payment record) exists even though the leading hypothesis isn't financial fraud. Run a lighter-weight financial trace to see whether it's a procurement trail (equipment/vehicle purchase) rather than the primary motive.
direction.trigger: Financial evidence exists in the case but no financial-fraud hypothesis is currently in the top-ranked list.
search_targets: Bank/UPI records tied to the referenced account or wallet
Recent large or unusual transactions near the incident date
cross_match: Transaction counterparties against suspects from the leading hypothesis
Transaction timing against procurement leads (e.g. equipment vendors)
direction.expected_outcome: Either confirms the financial trail is procurement-related (supporting the leading hypothesis) or surfaces a separate financial motive worth its own hypothesis.
failure_conditions: No unusual transactions near incident date

rules.why_template: Financial evidence exists but isn't yet the leading theory — a light-weight check avoids missing a procurement or secondary-motive trail.
